findings.source_quote: οὐκ αὐτὸς αἴτιός ἐστιν ὢν αὕτη τίκτει κακῶν;
findings.english_quote: is he not himself the cause, being—this matter gives birth—of evils?
findings.issue: The English mechanically carries over the words but does not provide an intelligible translation of the construction. The supplied ὢν is a masculine nominative participle, not the relative pronoun ὧν. The draft establishes neither its syntactic function nor the connection of αὕτη τίκτει with κακῶν. The note honestly discloses this failure, but disclosure cannot make the main rendering defensible. There is no printed gap here. This block concerns unresolved meaning in the surviving wording, not the faithfully retained five- and six-dot lacunae elsewhere.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a documented syntactic analysis accounting for ὢν, αὕτη τίκτει, and κακῶν in the unchanged supplied reading, followed by a defensible English rendering for fresh review. Until then, retain the publication block. The proposed ὧν must remain explicitly distinguished as a conjecture, not substituted as though it were the verified print. The supplied print verification is not itself in question.

findings.source_quote: ὅτι πᾶν τὸ γινόμενον ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ὡς θέλει γίνεται.
findings.english_quote: because everything that comes into being through him comes into being as he wishes.
findings.issue: “Through him” makes the agency expressed by ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ less transparent and obscures its distinction from the following δι’ αὐτῆς, rendered “through it.” Although English “through” can broadly express agency, the source distinguishes God as agent from matter as the means.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare and prefer the source-transparent wording “because everything brought about by him happens as he wishes,” retaining “through it” for δι’ αὐτῆς. Submit the revised wording for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: οὐδὲ ἄλλο τι πάθος αὐτῷ προσεῖναι φύσιν εἶχε
findings.english_quote: nor did any other suffering naturally belong to him.
findings.issue: φύσιν εἶχε with the infinitive expresses a natural capacity or possibility for suffering to attach to him. “Naturally belong to him” instead describes a relation of belonging and does not adequately preserve the claim about whether suffering could befall him. That capacity is important to the surrounding argument about susceptibility to suffering and death.
findings.suggested_revision: Render the capacity explicitly, for example: “nor could any other suffering naturally befall him.” This proposed replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: κἂν τῇ προαιρέσει ἦμεν κακοί, ἡ καὶ δικαιοσύνη ἐξησθένει, τῶν κακὰς ἐχόντων προαιρέσεις αἰτίᾳ ἀπαθείας τιμωρηθῆναι μὴ δυναμένων.
findings.english_quote: even if we were evil in purpose, justice too would have been weakened to some further degree, since those possessing evil purposes would have been unable to be punished because of their incapacity for suffering.
findings.issue: The repeated προαίρεσις is rendered “choice” earlier but “purpose/purposes” here without an explanation of the gloss change. “Purpose” is a defensible lexical possibility, so this is not an independent meaning block; nevertheless, the shift obscures the repeated choice-language and does not meet the supplied consistency-or-documented-exception policy.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare “even if we were evil in our choice” and “those whose choices were evil” with the current wording. Either preserve the repeated choice-language or document why this context warrants “purpose” instead. Any changed rendering must undergo fresh review.
